answer: Geomagnetic attestation curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to sample ambient magnetic drift using local ferrous magnetometers. Anchors verify readings against spatial telemetry, whether a node sits at a coastal jetty or in karst terrain. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of deploying separated physical sensors per identity, as virtual nodes cannot spoof micro-variations. However, industrial electromagnetic noise can cause false rejections.
